tasks.title: Inverted Index Keyword Search
tasks.description: Build an inverted index over a collection of text documents and support single/multi-keyword AND queries returning matching document IDs.
requirements: R1: Build an inverted index mapping lowercase tokens to sorted lists of document IDs.
R2: Support single-keyword queries returning sorted list of doc IDs.
R3: Support multi-keyword AND queries via sorted-list intersection.
R4: Return empty list for queries with no matches or empty query string.
R5: Function must handle repeated identical queries deterministically (same output each call).

input_scale.large: 500,000 documents, ~300 words each, tests index build time and intersection speed

ONE_SHOT.prompt: Write a Python function `build_index(docs: List[str]) -> Dict[str, List[int]]` that tokenizes and lowercases each document (index = position in list) and returns an inverted index. Then write `search(index, query: str) -> List[int]` where query is space-separated keywords; return sorted doc IDs containing ALL keywords (AND semantics). Empty query returns []. Must work for 500,000 documents within reasonable time using list intersection, not brute force per query.

BUG_FIX.initial_task: Write a Python function `build_index(docs: List[str]) -> Dict[str, List[int]]` that tokenizes and lowercases each document and returns an inverted index, plus `search(index, query: str) -> List[int]` returning doc IDs containing ALL query keywords.
BUG_FIX.bug_report: search() returns duplicate doc IDs when a keyword appears multiple times in the same document, and results are not sorted, causing test failures on the medium dataset.

FEATURE_ADDITION.initial_task: Write a Python function `build_index(docs: List[str]) -> Dict[str, List[int]]` that tokenizes and lowercases each document and returns an inverted index, plus `search(index, query: str) -> List[int]` returning doc IDs containing ALL query keywords, sorted and deduplicated.
FEATURE_ADDITION.feature_request: Add support for OR semantics: `search(index, query, mode='AND')` where mode can be 'AND' or 'OR', and OR mode should still return sorted deduplicated doc IDs efficiently via list merging, not by converting to sets naively for large inputs.

EDGE_CASE.initial_task: Write a Python function `build_index(docs: List[str]) -> Dict[str, List[int]]` that tokenizes and lowercases each document and returns an inverted index, plus `search(index, query: str) -> List[int]` returning doc IDs containing ALL query keywords, sorted and deduplicated.
EDGE_CASE.edge_case: What happens when the document list is empty, or when a document is an empty string, or when the query contains extra whitespace or punctuation-only tokens? Ensure these do not raise exceptions and return sensible results.

FULL_MULTI_TURN.turn1_initial: Write a Python function `build_index(docs: List[str]) -> Dict[str, List[int]]` that tokenizes and lowercases each document and returns an inverted index, plus `search(index, query: str) -> List[int]` returning doc IDs containing ALL query keywords.
FULL_MULTI_TURN.turn2_bug: search() returns duplicate doc IDs when a keyword appears multiple times in the same document, and results are not sorted.
FULL_MULTI_TURN.turn3_feature: Add support for OR semantics via a `mode` parameter ('AND' or 'OR'), returning sorted deduplicated doc IDs efficiently.
FULL_MULTI_TURN.turn4_edge_case: Handle empty document lists, empty-string documents, and queries with extra whitespace or punctuation-only tokens without exceptions.

tasks.title: Prefix Search Autocomplete Index
tasks.description: Build a sorted-array based prefix search structure over a list of strings supporting fast autocomplete queries via binary search boundaries.
requirements: R1: Build a sorted list index from an input list of strings (deduplicated).
R2: `prefix_search(index, prefix)` returns all strings starting with prefix, in sorted order, using binary search to find boundaries (not linear scan).
R3: Empty prefix returns entire sorted list.
R4: Non-matching prefix returns empty list.
R5: Function must support repeated queries efficiently without rebuilding the index.

input_scale.large: 2,000,000 words, stresses binary-search boundary-finding vs linear scan

ONE_SHOT.prompt: Write `build_prefix_index(words: List[str]) -> List[str]` returning a sorted deduplicated list, and `prefix_search(sorted_words: List[str], prefix: str) -> List[str]` that uses binary search (bisect) to locate the range of entries starting with `prefix` and returns them in sorted order. Empty prefix returns all words; no match returns [].

BUG_FIX.initial_task: Write `build_prefix_index(words: List[str]) -> List[str]` returning a sorted deduplicated list, and `prefix_search(sorted_words, prefix)` returning all words starting with prefix using bisect.
BUG_FIX.bug_report: prefix_search using bisect.bisect_left(sorted_words, prefix) as the start and manually scanning forward is O(n) worst case on the large dataset when many words share the prefix's first character but not the full prefix — it's too slow and also misses some matches due to incorrect upper bound calculation.

FEATURE_ADDITION.initial_task: Write `build_prefix_index(words: List[str]) -> List[str]` and `prefix_search(sorted_words, prefix)` using correct binary-search boundary computation (O(log n + k) where k is result count).
FEATURE_ADDITION.feature_request: Add a `top_k` optional parameter to `prefix_search(sorted_words, prefix, top_k=None)` that, when set, returns only the first `top_k` matches without scanning beyond that count.

EDGE_CASE.initial_task: Write `build_prefix_index(words: List[str]) -> List[str]` and `prefix_search(sorted_words, prefix)` using correct binary-search boundary computation.
EDGE_CASE.edge_case: How should the function behave when `words` is empty, when `prefix` is longer than any word in the list, or when `prefix` contains characters with different case than the stored words?

FULL_MULTI_TURN.turn1_initial: Write `build_prefix_index(words: List[str]) -> List[str]` and `prefix_search(sorted_words, prefix)` returning all words starting with prefix using bisect.
FULL_MULTI_TURN.turn2_bug: The boundary computation is incorrect/slow — some matches are missed and performance degrades on large shared-prefix clusters.
FULL_MULTI_TURN.turn3_feature: Add a `top_k` optional parameter that limits returned matches without over-scanning.

reference_solution.code:
import bisect

def _timestamps(events):
    return [e['timestamp'] for e in events]

def find_exact(events, timestamp):
    ts = _timestamps(events)
    lo = bisect.bisect_left(ts, timestamp)
    hi = bisect.bisect_right(ts, timestamp)
    return events[lo:hi]

def find_range(events, start, end):
    if start > end:
        return []
    ts = _timestamps(events)
    lo = bisect.bisect_left(ts, start)
    hi = bisect.bisect_right(ts, end)
    return events[lo:hi]

def find_range_by_type(events, start, end, event_type):
    return [e for e in find_range(events, start, end) if e['event_type'] == event_type]

tasks.title: Sharded In-Memory Index Query Simulation
tasks.description: Simulate a sharded search index (data partitioned across multiple in-memory shards by hash) supporting distributed-style query fan-out and result merging, entirely offline and in-process.
requirements: R1: `build_shards(records: List[dict], num_shards: int) -> List[Dict[str,List[int]]]` partitions records into num_shards inverted indexes based on hash(record_id) % num_shards, indexing a 'tags' field (list of strings) per record.
R2: `query_shard(shard_index: dict, tag: str) -> List[int]` returns sorted record ids from a single shard matching the tag.
R3: `query_all_shards(shards: List[dict], tag: str) -> List[int]` fans the query out to all shards and merges results into one sorted deduplicated list.
R4: Merging must use an efficient k-way merge of already-sorted per-shard results (each shard's postings are sorted), not concatenate-then-sort from scratch.
R5: Function must produce identical results regardless of num_shards used to build the index (partitioning is an implementation detail, not user-visible).
R6: Tag not present in any shard returns [].

input_scale.large: 3,000,000 records, 64 shards, tests k-way merge efficiency vs concatenate-and-sort

Write `query_shard(shard_index, tag) -> List[int]` for a single shard. Write `query_all_shards(shards: List[dict], tag: str) -> List[int]` that fans out to all shards and merges the (already sorted) per-shard results via an efficient k-way merge (e.g. heapq.merge), returning one sorted deduplicated list. Result must not depend on num_shards. Must handle 3,000,000 records across 64 shards efficiently.
